text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose slightly today in a market shaped by geopolitical oil supply concerns. The Saudi pipeline shutdown announced over the weekend, combined with ongoing tensions in the Iran war and Russia-Ukraine conflict, has kept crude prices elevated (US oil at $97/barrel, world oil at $109/barrel) and US refineries running at near-full capacity (97.8%). With refineries operating near their limits and crude supplies constrained by regional conflicts, refiners like Marathon benefit from wider profit margins on each barrel processed.

The broader tailwind for the sector comes from the Trump administration's rollback of climate regulations on power plants, which removes a regulatory headwind for fossil fuel operations. Over the past two weeks, the stock has climbed 7.5%, reflecting investor confidence that geopolitical turmoil and lighter regulation will sustain high refining activity and energy demand.
